question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}{e}^{-(\frac{x}{2}+2y)}, & x\ge 0,\,y\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(Y>2).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are two continuous random variables with joint probability density function $f(x,y),$ then the marginal density functions for $X$ and $Y$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X}(x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}y,\,{f}_{Y}(y)={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }f(x,y)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, the marginal density function of $Y$ for $y\ge 0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(y) & ={\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-(\frac{x}{2}+2y)}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-2{e}^{-(\frac{x}{2}+2y)}]}_{x=0}^{x=\infty } \\  & =-2(0-{e}^{-(0+2y)}) \\  & =2{e}^{-2y}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the full expression for ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is given by

$$
{f}_{Y}(y)=\{\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2y}, & y\ge 0, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required probability is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y>2) & ={\int }_{2}^{\infty }{f}_{Y}(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{\infty }2{e}^{-2y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[-{e}^{-2y}]}_{2}^{\infty } \\  & =(0+{e}^{-4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{{e}^{4}}.\end{aligned}
$$
